title: Portable Trusted Linux
summary: Portable Trusted Linux is a portable security environment designed to boot independently of an installed operating system, authenticate its own trusted components, collect hardware-backed boot evidence where available, run with minimal persistence, produce independently verifiable attestation records, and preserve the history of those records through cryptographic evidence anchoring. Prototype 1 is now moving from architecture into a staged Debian 13/trixie build pipeline.

sections.title: Project objective
sections.content: Portable Trusted Linux addresses the circular-trust problem created when an already-installed operating system may be compromised. The project boots independently from authenticated portable media and builds confidence in separately testable stages instead of issuing a simplistic SAFE/UNSAFE result.

sections.title: Runtime trust chain
sections.content: The target chain is: authenticated release reference -> verified USB image -> UEFI/Secure Boot -> measured boot and TCG event log -> TPM PCR evidence -> signed UKI -> authenticated dm-verity root -> immutable Linux -> RAM-backed session -> nonce-bound TPM Quote -> independent verifier -> attestation report.

sections.title: Prototype 1 build baseline
sections.content: Prototype 1 targets Debian 13 trixie on amd64/x86-64. Current Debian package metadata confirms that trixie provides live-build, systemd-ukify and tpm2-tools, while the live-build package itself includes a dm-verity build component. The repository now contains a staged dependency installer, host preflight, live-build runner, artifact manifest generator and static validation script. Exact package versions are captured from the real build host rather than assumed permanently from the moving Debian repository.

sections.title: Build provenance versus authenticity
sections.content: The generated build manifest records an artifact SHA-256, file size, source Git commit, builder identity and selected package versions. This is provenance evidence about how a file was produced; it is not yet proof that an external user should trust that release. Release signing is deliberately kept as a separate future security gate.

sections.title: TPM and attestation
sections.content: TPM 2.0 evidence is treated as evidence requiring verification rather than a self-issued SAFE result. The target attester produces nonce-bound Quote evidence over selected PCRs and supplies the TCG event log. The independent verifier evaluates signatures, freshness, PCR selection, log consistency and reference policy.

sections.title: Immutable runtime
sections.content: The trusted root is intended to be read-only and protected by dm-verity. Normal writable state will be separated into a RAM-backed layer so ordinary session changes disappear after shutdown unless deliberately exported.

sections.title: Evidence history
sections.content: Attestation evidence is designed as a deterministic payload plus an outer envelope. The payload is canonicalised and hashed; the envelope carries the payload digest, signatures and future external-anchor receipts. This prevents a self-referential report-hash design and supports later hash chaining and transparency-log anchoring.

sections.title: Safety boundary
sections.content: The project intentionally does not yet include a raw USB-writing script. Destructive media writing will only be added after target-device safety checks and negative tests can prove that ambiguous, internal or otherwise unsafe devices are refused by default. Random-PC mode also avoids silent Secure Boot key enrollment, TPM clearing, firmware changes or writes to internal disks.

sections.title: Mandatory lessons-learned discipline
sections.content: Every meaningful engineering session, research finding, failure or architecture surprise must be recorded in docs/07-lessons-learned.md, propagated into affected specifications or decisions, and followed by a final update to project_content.json. This rule is part of PROJECT_RULES.md and the Architecture Decision Register.

sections.title: Current next step
sections.content: Run tests/00-static-check.sh and build/00-host-check.sh on a clean Debian 13/trixie amd64 machine, install the packaged dependencies, rerun preflight, then execute the first Debian Live build. Preserve the real command output and record every unexpected result before moving on to UKI, dm-verity and TPM integration.

decisions.title: Reuse mature security components
decisions.text: Use Debian, UEFI Secure Boot, systemd UKI, TPM 2.0 and dm-verity rather than inventing replacement security primitives.

decisions.title: Independent verification is mandatory
decisions.text: The target computer cannot be the sole authority deciding that its own measurements are trustworthy.

decisions.title: External Evidence Anchoring added
decisions.text: Attestation history supports hashing, signatures, previous-report linkage and later external commitments, with transparency logs preferred and blockchain optional.

decisions.title: GitHub is the canonical development workspace
decisions.text: Documents, source and the living JSON index are versioned in the private repository.

decisions.title: Lessons learned are mandatory output
decisions.text: Every meaningful engineering session must record lessons before project_content.json is updated last.

decisions.title: Prototype 1 baseline is Debian 13/trixie amd64
decisions.text: Exact point release and package versions are recorded as build provenance.

decisions.title: Attestation reports use payload plus envelope
decisions.text: The deterministic payload is hashed and an outer envelope carries digest, signatures and future anchor receipts.

decisions.title: Build provenance is separate from release authenticity
decisions.text: A detailed unsigned manifest does not authenticate a release; signing remains a separate gate.

decisions.title: No destructive USB writer before safety tests
decisions.text: Raw media writing waits until device-refusal checks and negative tests protect internal or ambiguous storage targets.
